column3: A fountain of the Merlion, a half-lion, half-fish figure that is the symbol of Singapore, spouting water into the bay in front of the city skyline.
A hotel of three towers topped by a ship-shaped rooftop with an infinity pool and a view across Marina Bay.
A garden by the bay with giant Supertrees, steel tree-like structures covered in plants, that light up at night. Two glass domes hold cool-weather plants.
Chinatown is an old district of shophouses, temples and food stalls, with lanterns and busy markets.
A large temple in Tang-dynasty style that houses a relic said to be a tooth of the Buddha.
A colorful area of Indian shops, temples and restaurants, with garlands, spices, silk and the smell of curry.
The Malay quarter of Singapore, with Arab Street, textile shops, cafés and the Sultan Mosque.
A mosque with a golden dome, the biggest in Singapore, and the heart of the Malay-Muslim community.
The river where Singapore's trade began, lined with old warehouses that are now restaurants and bars, and crossed by bridges.
A famous shopping street with malls, department stores and fashion brands, lit up in bright festive lights at Christmas.
The oldest museum in the country, with a neoclassical building, which tells the story of Singapore from its early days.
A garden of old trees, lakes and orchids, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the only tropical garden with this status.
A colonial hotel, opened in 1887, where the Singapore Sling cocktail was created. It is a white building with palms and verandas.
Poached chicken with rice cooked in chicken stock, with chili, ginger and dark soy. It is considered the national dish of Singapore.
A whole crab stir-fried in a sweet and spicy tomato-chili sauce, with an egg ribbon. You eat it with your hands, and use fried buns to soak up the sauce.
A coconut curry noodle soup with prawns, fish cake and cockles, a Peranakan classic.
Toast with coconut jam and butter, served with soft-boiled eggs and sweet coffee, a traditional breakfast.
Pork rib soup with lots of pepper and garlic, eaten with rice and fried dough, in a rich, peppery broth.
Flat rice noodles fried over high heat with egg, cockles, Chinese sausage and sweet soy sauce, with a smoky aroma.
Skewers of marinated meat grilled over charcoal and served with a peanut sauce, rice cakes and cucumber.
Egg and rice noodles stir-fried with prawns, squid and pork in a rich shrimp stock.
A crispy omelet of oysters, egg and starch, served with chili sauce. A favorite hawker dish.
A pink cocktail with gin, cherry liqueur and pineapple juice, which was first mixed at the Raffles Hotel.
Open-air food courts with dozens of stalls offering cheap, delicious dishes. Singapore's hawker culture is on UNESCO's list of intangible heritage.
Chinese, Malay, Indian and other communities live side by side, and their festivals and foods are a part of daily life.
Singlish is a local English mixed with Chinese, Malay and Tamil, with short sentences and the particle lah.
Singapore's National Day on August 9 is celebrated with parades, flypasts and fireworks over the bay.
Deepavali is the Hindu festival of lights, when Little India is hung with lights and decorations.
A theme park on Sentosa Island, with movie-themed rides and shows.
A large aquarium with thousands of sea animals, including a huge viewing window into an ocean habitat.
A lively beach on Sentosa, with beach bars, volleyball courts and a view of passing ships.
A long seaside park with cycling paths, beaches and seafood restaurants, a favorite place for weekend outings.
A garden mall at Changi Airport, with a 40-meter indoor waterfall, known as the Rain Vortex, surrounded by trees and shops.
A small island that keeps the old village life, where you can cycle on dirt paths through forests and mangroves.
Colorful steamed cakes made of rice flour, coconut and pandan, the sweets of the Peranakan community.
Rice cooked in coconut milk and served with fried fish, anchovies, egg and spicy sambal, a Malay breakfast favorite.
A curry noodle soup from Katong, with short noodles that you can eat with a spoon alone.
A bird park with thousands of colorful birds, including a large walk-in aviary and bird shows.
A garden of Chinese design with pagodas, bridges and a pond, a quiet place by the lake.
A Japanese garden with stone paths, bridges and ponds, and quiet corners for rest.
A university with a modern campus, with large green spaces and an unusual building shaped like a stack of round plates.
A zoo where many animals live in open enclosures without bars, and visitors can have breakfast with orangutans.
The world's first nocturnal zoo, where you can walk or ride a tram through dim forests to see animals that are awake at night.
Durian is called the king of fruits, with a strong smell, a creamy flesh and a very sweet taste. It is banned on public transport in Singapore.
